clue.text: Document required for transferring estate car?

definitions.meaning: the legal deed by which property passes from seller to buyer
a car is a vehicle, a means of carrying people; the question mark flags it as an example

explanation.surface: Someone asks what paperwork is needed to sell a family estate car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estate car' reads as one thing, a station wagon; split it, so 'estate' belongs to the property deed and 'car' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, the deed transferring land is so called; in general use the word means any vehicle.

clue.text: Vices shown by person elected in short order

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
short means the word for order loses its last letter

parts.note: an order is a rank or class, as in the lower orders
an MP, Member of Parliament, is elected

explanation.surface: An elected politician is shown up for his vices in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short order' looks like a phrase meaning quickly; split it: 'short' trims order's word and 'in' places the politician inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vices (US vises) are workbench tools that grip, the same job as clamps.

clue.text: Food from Mexico boy set up outside a church

indicators.note: outside means the reversed piece wraps round the others
in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a boy is a son

explanation.surface: A Mexican boy has set up a food stall outside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' signals reversal because in a down entry the word reads upwards; 'outside' wraps it round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortilla chips with melted cheese are a Mexican dish, served as a snack.

clue.text: Improve and take lad off for a drink

indicators.note: off means the letters are gone wrong, thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is told to shape up and take the young man out for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take lad off' reads as an instruction; 'and' is a link and 'off' shuffles IMPROVE, TAKE and LAD together.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentrated tinned milk can be drunk or added to drinks, a loose but fair use of drink.

clue.text: Bill locks ladies in green room, perhaps

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
locks of hair are tresses

explanation.surface: A man called Bill shuts some women inside a green room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name and 'locks' like a verb; they are an account and hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers wait in a theatre's green room before going on stage, so women there may be stage performers.

clue.text: Check weapon for magnetism

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: Someone checks a weapon for magnetic properties.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal magnetism is attractiveness, the power to draw people in.

clue.text: Check containers on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means the word is read in the return direction, backwards

parts.note: pots are containers

explanation.surface: Someone inspects the containers on the return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to halt or arrest it.

clue.text: Story after count will be revealing

indicators.note: after means the story's word comes behind the count's word

parts.note: to tell is to count, as a bank teller does
a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A narrator promises the story will reveal everything after the count.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale sign is one that gives something away, revealing it.

clue.text: Left on boat with temperature missing elegance shown by ocean dweller

indicators.note: missing means the temperature letter is taken away

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
poise is graceful elegance

explanation.surface: A graceful sea creature appears to the left of a boat in falling temperatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing' drops the T from PORT, leaving POR.
explanation.definitionFit: A small toothed whale lives in the sea, so it fits a descriptive name for a marine creature.

clue.text: They may hold up lines of communication

definitions.text: They may hold up lines of communication

parts.words: They may hold up lines of communication
parts.note: hold up reads as delay, but these wooden supports literally carry the overhead wires of a phone network

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' suggests obstruction; the sense is physical support of cables.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall wooden posts carry the overhead wires along which messages travel.

clue.text: Insomniac crackpot's accommodating city

indicators.note: accommodating means the phrase holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A sleepless eccentric's city makes room for him.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Ghana is a West African city.

clue.text: Bank employee gets hold of artist — very representative

indicators.note: gets hold of means the first word grips the others inside it

parts.note: a teller works at a bank counter
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A bank clerk grabs an artist who is very representative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets hold of' makes the bank employee's word the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial salesman on the road is a sales representative.

clue.text: Advertise concert, anticipating on-target earnings

indicators.note: anticipating means coming before, so the concert's word goes first

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert
OTE is the jobs-advert abbreviation for on-target earnings

explanation.surface: An advert for a concert job, with talk of on-target earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: OTE appears in British sales job adverts as expected pay with bonuses.
explanation.definitionFit: To advertise a product is to publicise it and push its sales.

clue.text: Comfort seamstress hugging returning expert

indicators.note: returning means the held letters are read backwards
hugging means the two words hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A seamstress is comforted with a hug by a returning expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hugging' picks ORTSEAM from comfORT SEAMstress; 'returning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A master or virtuoso, especially in music, is an expert.

clue.text: Wise man touring America registers snack food

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the sage word surrounds America

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
USA is America
rolls are registers or lists of names

explanation.surface: A wise man on a tour of America writes down snacks in his ledgers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touring' means the wise man goes round America.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry-wrapped sausage meat is a classic British snack, eaten cold or warm.

clue.text: Couple propping up the bar at football?

definitions.text: Couple propping up the bar at football?

parts.words: Couple propping up the bar at football?
parts.note: a pair of drinkers leaning on a pub bar, or the two uprights supporting the crossbar of a goal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Propping up the bar' is slang for drinking in a pub; here the bar is the goal's crossbar.
explanation.definitionFit: Two uprights hold up a goal's crossbar in football.

clue.text: Takes unfair advantage of Democrat taken in by jittery senator

indicators.note: taken in by means the Democrat letter goes inside the other piece
jittery means nervous and shaky, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A nervous senator is fooled by a Democrat colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jittery' scrambles SENATOR and D goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit a reputation or a relationship is to cash in on it unfairly.

clue.text: Stubborn, and planning bad route

indicators.note: planning means working the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly plans a bad route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planning' reshuffles BAD ROUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: obstinate, unyielding, refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: Gives approval for bit of bridge needing impressions

parts.note: a rubber is a unit of play in the card game bridge
stamps are impressions pressed onto paper

explanation.surface: A section of bridge needs stamps impressed on it before approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' suggests a structure; it is the card game, in which a rubber is a set of games.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to approve something automatically, without real scrutiny.

clue.text: Plant a tree across lake

indicators.note: across means the first pieces span the lake letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a pine is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone plants a tree on the far side of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountain plants grown in rock gardens are named for the Alps.

clue.text: Accept honour

definitions.meaning: to believe or trust a claim
praise or recognition for something done, as in getting the merit for it

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers believing a story and the recognition due for an achievement.

clue.text: 22's doctor needing season to start late

indicators.note: late means dead or gone, so the season's first letter is no longer there

parts.note: summer is a season

explanation.surface: A musician's doctor needs the season to begin later.
explanation.walkthrough: '22's' reads as 22 is; 22 is Ringo, the Beatles' percussionist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr played the drums for the Beatles, so he is an example of a percussion player.

clue.text: Percussionist must have love to support band

parts.note: a ring is a band, as worn on a finger
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A drummer insists on love to back up the group.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry O sits below RING, supporting it, though 'to support' is a joining phrase here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr was the Beatles' famous drummer, a percussion player.

clue.text: Mass-market power with uranium found in Arctic environment

indicators.note: found in means the pieces sit within the other word

parts.note: polar describes the Arctic region
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Mass-market nuclear power appears in the Arctic.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass-market goods appeal to a broad public, the very sense of widely liked.

clue.text: Celebrities will eat fish — they flock together

indicators.note: will eat means the stars word takes the fish inside it

parts.note: celebrities are stars
a ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Famous people will dine on fish when they gather together.
explanation.definitionFit: These birds gather in huge murmurations, flocks of thousands.

clue.text: Landowner left daughter taking in broadcast

indicators.note: taking in means the two letters surround the broadcast word

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A landowner leaves his daughter tuned in to a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish estate owner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish word for a lord of an estate means a landholder.

clue.text: Votes against hooter being sounded

indicators.note: being sounded means the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: hooter is slang for a nose

explanation.surface: Votes against a car horn being sounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' looks like a horn; it is slang for the face's nose.
explanation.definitionFit: In parliamentary divisions those voting no are counted as such.

clue.text: Happy to accept son is dependable

indicators.note: to accept means the happy word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: content means happy

explanation.surface: A cheerful parent welcomes a son who is reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To accept' makes the happy word the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: reliable, steady, always behaving the same way.
